'''Robert Stuart Doran''' (born December 21, 1937) is an American [[mathematician]]. He held the John William and Helen Stubbs Potter Professorship in mathematics at [[Texas Christian University|Texas Christian University (TCU)]] from 1995 until his retirement in 2016. Doran served as chair of the TCU mathematics department for 21 years.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Doran Selected for Potter Mathematics Professorship|journal=The Next Frontier Magazine of Texas Christian University|date=Summer 1995|volume=21|issue=3|page=4}}</ref>  He has also held visiting appointments at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], the [[University of Oxford]], and the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, N.J.]] He was elected to the board of trustees of the Association of Members of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], serving as president of the organization for 10 years.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Mathematician named trustee of the Institute for Advanced Study|journal=Texas Christian University: Research Bulletin|date=Fall 1986|pages=7–8}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Community of Scholars|date=9 December 2019|url=http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/users/1554}}</ref>  He has been an editor for the ''Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications'', [[Cambridge University Press]], a position he has held since 1988.<ref>Cambridge Core. "Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications." Cambridge University Press. https://www.cambridge.org/core/series/encyclopedia-of-mathematics-and-its-applications/14161A9F36D6D0C9A650A4F86F74162D</ref> Doran is known for his research-level books, his award-winning teaching, and for his solution to a long-standing open problem due to [[Irving Kaplansky]] on a [[Symmetric algebra|symmetric *-algebra]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Doran|first=Robert|title=A Generalization of a theorem of Civin and Yood|journal=Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society|year=1972|volume=4|pages=25–26|doi=10.1112/blms/4.1.25}}</ref>

== Personal background ==
Robert Stuart Doran was born on December 21, 1937, in [[Winthrop, Iowa]].<ref>"Winthrop." MapSof.net. https://www.mapsof.net/winthrop-ia</ref> In 1959, he married Shirley Ann Lange. They have two sons, Bruce and Brad.

;Military service
In 1956, Doran served in the [[82nd Airborne Division]] at [[Fort Bragg, North Carolina]]. He served as a [[Special Forces]] Instructor at the US Army Jungle Survival Center at [[Fort Sherman|Fort Sherman, Colón, Panama]].<ref name="Andersen 12–13">{{cite journal|last=Andersen|first=Nancy|title=A Formula For More Than Math|journal=Image Magazine|date=October 1986|pages=12–13}}</ref>  He left active duty in the military in 1958 and he served in the [[US Army]] reserves until 1962 when he was honorably discharged.

;Educational background
Doran, a member of Phi Beta Kappa, studied mathematics at the [[University of Iowa]] from 1959 until 1964, earning a [[Bachelor's degree]] and a [[Master of Science]] degree. He received a Ph.D in mathematics from the [[University of Washington]] in 1968, under the direction of [[James Michael Gardner Fell|J. M. G. Fell]] and [https://sites.math.washington.edu/~gangolli/ Ramesh Gangolli].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=11316|title = Robert Doran - the Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref> His doctoral dissertation,<ref>{{cite journal|last=Doran|first=Robert|title=Construction of uniform CT-bundles|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|year=1968|volume=15|pages=551}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Doran|first=Robert|title=Representations of C*-algebras by Uniform CT bundles and Operator theory|year=1968|publisher=University of Washington}}</ref> titled Representations of C*-algebras by Uniform CT-bundles and Operator Theory, dealt with topological representations in spaces of cross-sections of [[fiber bundle]]s of a non-commutative [[C*-algebra]]. This work was motivated in part by the classical [[Gelfand–Naimark theorem]] for [[C*-algebras]] and by the work of [[Masamichi Takesaki|M. Takesaki]] and J. Tomiyama.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Tomiyama|first=J.|author2=M. Takesaki |title=Applications of fiber bundles to a certain class of C*-algebras|journal=Tohoku Math J|year=1961|volume=13|pages=498–523|doi=10.2748/tmj/1178244253|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Tomiyama|first=J.|title=Topological representation of C*-algebras|journal=Tohoku Math J|year=1962|volume=14|pages=182–204|doi=10.2748/tmj/1178244174|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Professional background ==
Doran held the John William and Helen Stubbs Potter Professor of Mathematics at [[Texas Christian University]] from 1995 to 2016. He was faculty sponsor of the TCU chapter of [[Campus Crusade for Christ]] ([[Cru (Christian organization)|Cru]]) for 43 years, and he was the founding faculty sponsor in 1989 of the TCU chapter of [[Beta Upsilon Chi|Brothers Under Christ]] ([[Beta Upsilon Chi]]).

He has held visiting appointments at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (1980), [[Oxford University]] in England (1988), and the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] (1981).<ref name="ReferenceA">{{cite journal|title=Mathematician named trustee of the Institute for Advanced Study|journal=Texas Christian University: Research Bulletin|year=1986|pages=7–8}}</ref>  His areas of research involve [[representation theory]], [[C*-algebra]] characterizations, the notion of an [[approximate identity]] in a [[Banach algebra]], and [[Banach bundle]] theory.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Rieffel|author-link=Marc Rieffel|first=Marc|title=Reviews|journal=The American Mathematical Monthly|date=February 1990|volume=97|issue=2|pages=167–170|doi=10.2307/2323935|jstor=2323935}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Williams|first=Dana|title=Review: Representations of *-algebras, locally compact groups, and Banach *-algebraic bundles|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|year=1989|volume=21|issue=2|pages=311–314|doi=10.1090/s0273-0979-1989-15840-0|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Doran taught at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. In 1988 he published an article titled "A care package for undergraduate mathematics students" that outlined his teaching methods.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Doran|first=Robert|title=A Care Package for Undergraduate Mathematics Students|journal=Mathematics in College|year=1988|pages=32–37}}</ref> He has received national, statewide, and local awards for his teaching.<ref>{{cite journal|year=1990|title=National Teaching Awards to Mathematicians|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|volume=37|issue=1|page=27}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Past Recipients of the Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics Award|url=http://sections.maa.org/texas/awards|publisher=MAA Texas}}</ref>

Doran was chair of the TCU Mathematics Department for 21 years (1990–2011). In 1986 he was elected to the board of trustees the Association of Members of the Institute for Advanced Study.<ref name="ReferenceA"/>  He was president of the association for 10 years (1990-1999). Doran has been an editor for [[Cambridge University Press]] since 1988.<ref>{{cite web|title=Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications|url=http://www.cup.cam.ac.uk/aus/series/sSeries.asp?code=EOM|publisher=Cambridge University Press}}{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>  He has also organized many [[American Mathematical Society]] special sessions and conferences for CBMS, the [[Conference Board of the Mathematical Sciences]]. His first such conference was held at TCU in 1970 with [[Paul Halmos]] as principal speaker.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Halmos|first=P. R.|title=Ten problems in Hilbert space|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |volume=76|issue=5|pages=887–933|doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1970-12502-2|year=1970|doi-access=free}}</ref> The most recent conference was held at TCU, June 2011 with [[Phillip Griffiths]], former Director of the Institute for Advanced Study as principal speaker.

Doran is known for his elegant solution<ref>{{cite journal|last=Doran|first=R. S.|title=A generalization of a theorem of Civin and Yood|journal=Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society|year=1972|volume=4|pages=25–26|doi=10.1112/blms/4.1.25}}</ref> of a long-standing unsolved problem on a symmetric [[*-algebra]] left open by [[Irving Kaplansky]] in the ''[[Duke Mathematical Journal]]'' in 1949.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Kaplansky|first=I.|title=Normed algebras|journal=Duke Mathematical Journal|year=1949|volume=16|issue=3|pages=399–418|doi=10.1215/s0012-7094-49-01640-3}}</ref>

== Published works ==
Doran has published books, articles, and reviews on a variety of topics, often collaborating with other mathematicians, including [[J. M. G. Fell]], [[Richard Kadison]], [[Calvin C. Moore|Calvin Moore]], [[Jonathan Rosenberg (mathematician)|Jonathan Rosenberg]], [[Paul Sally]], [[Robert Zimmer]], and [[V. S. Varadarajan]].
